items.title: Police Still Searching for Family of Woman Who Died After Saturday Night Fall Into Lake Ontario
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel police still have not identified the woman who died after falling into Lake Ontario at Jack Darling Memorial Park over the weekend, as investigators work to locate and notify her next of kin. INsauga reports the woman was swept into the water Saturday night and rushed to hospital, where she was pronounced dead a short time later. Police said Monday morning that no further details, including her age, will be released until her family has been notified. Investigators have not said whether the woman was alone or with others before she ended up in the lake. INsauga notes Jack Darling Memorial Park covers more than 20 acres along the Lake Ontario shoreline a few kilometres west of Port Credit Harbour, near where the Credit River empties into the lake. The park is one of the city's largest and most popular waterfront green spaces, with picnic areas, tennis courts, a beach, a leash-free zone, a spray pad, two playgrounds and a stretch of the Waterfront Trail running through it.

items.title: Dixie Road Southbound Lanes Shut All Week for Peel Region Storm Sewer Work
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region has closed all southbound lanes of Dixie Road in Mississauga's east end this week while crews replace a section of storm sewer between Blundell Road and Caterpillar Road. INsauga reports the closure runs south of Dundas Street East and north of The Queensway East, and is scheduled to last through Friday. Mississauga Ward 1 Coun. Stephen Dasko told residents in an online notice that the work is happening night and day, covering a stretch from 80 metres south of Blundell Road to 180 metres north of Caterpillar Road. INsauga notes the project is one of several similar infrastructure upgrades already underway or planned across the city as aging pipes and sewers get replaced. A short distance west, INsauga reports Peel Region crews are also preparing to rehabilitate the Lower Cooksville Trunk Sewer, a system Mississauga Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla has described as critical infrastructure carrying wastewater from homes and businesses in the area to treatment facilities. That project is expected to bring partial park and trail closures along with construction noise and dust starting this summer.

items.title: Overnight Gardenview Crescent Fire Prompts Evacuations and Road Closures in Mississauga's West End
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga firefighters mounted a large emergency response to a house fire on Gardenview Crescent in the city's west end early Monday morning. The street sits near Winston Churchill Boulevard and Thomas Street, and Peel police said occupants of the affected home were evacuated, along with neighbouring residents as a precaution. INsauga reports the fire appeared to stay contained to a single residence even with the scale of the response. One person was taken to a trauma centre with minor smoke inhalation, according to police. INsauga notes crews closed roads in the area while responding, reflecting what police described as a large deployment of Mississauga firefighters to the scene. As of Monday morning, police said the fire appeared to have been fully contained to the one home, with no word yet on what caused it.

items.title: Motorcyclist Suffers Non-Life-Threatening Injuries in Sunday Evening Dundas Street Crash
items.summary: According to INsauga, a motorcyclist was taken to hospital after a two-vehicle crash on Dundas Street East near Southcreek Road, west of The West Mall, on Sunday evening. Peel Regional Police said the collision involved a car and a motorcycle. INsauga reports the motorcyclist, described as an adult male, suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Both vehicles involved remained at the scene while officers investigated, and lanes on Dundas Street were reduced during that time. INsauga notes that by Monday morning, police said the accident scene had been fully cleared. Investigators have not said what may have caused the collision.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Applications for 2026 Santa Claus Parade Floats and Volunteers
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, applications are now open for businesses, community groups, performers and volunteers who want to take part in this year's Santa Claus Parade. The city says the annual parade will kick off the holiday season in downtown Mississauga, alongside the opening of the city's largest outdoor ice rink and the lighting of the Christmas tree at Celebration Square. This year's parade carries the theme Sauga's Home for the Holidays, meant to showcase the traditions, cultures, stories and people that make the city feel like home, according to the announcement. The City of Mississauga says float and walking group applications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and close on September 30 or once the parade reaches capacity, whichever comes first. Volunteers are also being sought for roles including parade marshals, ambassadors and staging support, with those applications closing November 3, 2026. The city notes anyone interested can find more information and apply through the parade's webpage.

items.title: Nine People Cling to Capsized Boat in Rough Lake Ontario Waters Off Port Credit
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Peel police rescued nine people Saturday evening after their boat capsized in rough conditions near Port Credit Harbour Marina in Mississauga. Const. Tyler Bell-Morena, a Peel police spokesperson, told the Toronto Star that officers found the vessel flipped over roughly 50 metres south of the Ridgetown break wall, tossed by high winds and waves reaching two to three metres. Bell-Morena described the conditions as challenging, and said all nine people were found clinging to the overturned boat when officers arrived. The Toronto Star reports everyone involved suffered only minor abrasions, with no other injuries reported. Investigators said it remains unclear what type of boat was involved. Bell-Morena said the vessel was later located near rocks on the west side of the Credit River, but crews were unable to recover it because of hazardous weather conditions. The Canadian Coast Guard was notified of the incident, the Toronto Star reports.
